description.text: Agostino d'Ippona was born on 13 November 354 in the Roman colony of Tagaste (now Souk Ahras, Algeria), the son of a Roman father, Patrizio, and a Berber mother, Monica, who would later become a saint.  Educated in the local schools of Tagaste and later in Carthage, he studied rhetoric and law, but his early life was marked by a spiritual conflict between the paganism of his father and the Christian faith of his mother, whose influence eventually led him to convert to Christianity.

After a period of theological exploration that included a brief involvement with Manichaeism, Agostino converted to orthodox Christianity in 386, a turning point described as occurring in a garden in Milan.  He was ordained a priest in 391, became Bishop of Hippo in 395, and served until his death on 28 August 430.  During his episcopate he authored the influential *City of God*, defended the Church against the Donatists, and contributed to the development of monastic rules that would later inspire the Order of Saint Augustine.

curiosities.text: He was nicknamed the Doctor Gratiae, or Doctor of Grace, reflecting his theological emphasis on divine grace.
His autobiographical work, the *Confessions*, is one of the earliest and most detailed Christian autobiographies, offering insight into his spiritual journey.
Agostino played a key role in the Donatist controversy, arguing that the Church should be inclusive of repentant sinners and opposing the strict separation advocated by the Donatists.
